text:
alex: Quick question — can we temporarily shorten retention for the dev-trace-cache used by feature experiments? We want to run a one-off prune to 7d for this cache to reduce storage while we triage IR-3251. It's supposed to be PII-free, but want sign-off.

jamie: Do those traces ever include customer_id or email in any payload? If yes we need full erase review.

alex: Not in logs we send to the cache; payloads are obfuscated. There is a hashed customer_id field (`cust_id_hash`) but no raw emails. The hashing is sha256 without salt (ugh).

priya: Heads up — policy requires 30d default for traces unless you can prove no re-identification risk. Has the hash been treated as PII by legal? If not, still risky if unsalted.

alex: We can run a scrub to remove `cust_id_hash` before prune. Proposed command:

```
kubectl exec -it cache-job -- /app/scrub --pattern cust_id_hash --in-place
```

Would that be acceptable?

priya: That's better. I need a short PR with the scrub script + verification steps (hash lookup sample) and a brief risk assessment. I can sign off once that's in place. Also cc @secops for approval.

security-bot: Policy: Data Retention & Erasure v3 — https://redwood.internal/policies/retention. For one-off deletes, file request: https://redwood.internal/erase-requests. Required approvers: Security Lead + Data Privacy.

jamie: Who on secops can approve quickly? We have a rollout window tomorrow.

priya: I can approve as Security Lead if the PR includes: scrub script, unit test showing removed field, and a verification log sample. If Legal flags unsalted hashes, we may have to rotate tokens instead of prune.

alex: OK I'll open the PR now and ping when ready. Thx :thumbsup:
